Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, dense opacity in the right upper hemithorax with ill-defined inferior margins, which is characteristic of Pleuropulmonary Synovial Sarcoma (PPSS) that often presents as a large mass with heterogeneous density due to necrosis or hemorrhage. This appearance aligns with option A, whereas options describing sharp margins, spiculation, or calcification do not match the radiographic findings shown.
